rationale:
Evidence. The best raced design is iteration 3 (score 49.94): five sensors at y = 0.06 m, x = -0.03 to +0.03 m, 0.016 m footprint, kp 2.0, ki 0.1, kd 0.1, base_speed 1.4, wheel_track 0.12 m, last_direction. Every trial in every iteration ended off track with exactly one line-loss event, and max_error is censored near 0.061 m, just past the fixed 0.06 m limit. Iterations 0 and 2 gave identical per-track metrics while kp, ki, kd, base_speed and sensor layout all changed, so the controller does not reach the first loss. Iteration 4 (sensors at y = 0.08) gave no gain (49.73 vs 49.94). Iteration 5 (search_left) was slightly worse (48.70), so the recovery rule is not a clear improvement.

Critique handling. I accept the round-2 critique's main point that the kd = 0.05 change is probably a null result. Iterations 0 and 2 differed tenfold in kd and gave the same numbers, so I expect the same first loss here. I also accept that the derivative kick at a tape edge is larger than my earlier estimate, because the full sensor-weight swing of about 1.5 per 10 ms gives a kd-scaled kick of roughly 15 turn units at kd 0.1. Halving kd reduces that kick, so the test still isolates the derivative term from the rest of the design. I partly accept the critique's request for a stronger test: this round stays a one-variable change, so any result is attributable. I reject the request to switch to a start-alignment or line_loss test now. Those tests change behaviour that the current evidence does not yet exclude, and they would need a separate round. I keep base_speed at 1.4 because no run has reached a progress level where speed is the limit, and speed has no completion evidence either way. I keep the raced geometry and the other gains unchanged.

Change. kd 0.1 to 0.05, a single variable from iteration 3.

Falsifiable expectation. If the first-loss step, progress, and max_error are unchanged to four decimals on all three tracks, the derivative term is ruled out and the next round should test start alignment or the line_loss rule. If progress or max_error moves by more than the seed spread (about 0.01 progress on the oval), derivative action was contributing and kd should be tuned again. The first-loss step itself is not returned by the requested measurements, so I read the change through progress, max_error, steering_oscillation and line_loss_events.
